propositions: _recall_false_accept computes specificity (fraction of safe items NOT blocked) but consumes it as an error rate (lower-is-better), inverting the gate logic and causing correct candidates to fail
The false_accept ceiling at max_false_accept=0.10 is effectively always-fail for any competent gate because the inverted metric scores high-quality runs near 1.0
Recorded live run (frontier slot) incorrectly failed with false-accept rise 0.143 when Bedrock achieved 14.3pp improvement in false-positive rate over Anthropic

The fix redefines false_accept computation to blocked/safe (wrongly-blocked rate, lower-is-better error) without changing comparison directions, aligning with existing metric definitions in eval.py and docs
A prerequisite gold fixture had encoded contradictory labels (advisory safe + must-block) that were only survivable under the inverted metric, requiring relabeling to reflect intent
